Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP status, including 5-year post-office residual risk treatment; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence must be obtained. Full MLRO or compliance officer sign-off required for any medium-risk non-face-to-face client onboarding for a video chat social app. Sanctions screening must be refreshed on a continuous or event-triggered basis, with independent audit trail.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House online name reservation portal (via the Financial Services Commission/Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar; online filing system under the Companies Act 2014)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Gibraltar law (English language jurisdiction) requires proposed company names to be in respect of the English alphabet only; the name may be in English but must not use symbols, special characters, or non-Latin scripts unless specifically approved by the Registrar; the name must be distinguishable from existing names and must include a legal element indicator such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'PLC', or equivalent; Gibraltar's company register operates exclusively in English, and any foreign-language names or transliterations must be transliterated into Latin characters and substantiated by a notarized translation or an official registry search certificate.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Royal, Crown, Imperial, Sovereign, Queen, King, Prince, Princess, Duke, Duchess, Her Majesty's, Government
Assurance, Bank, Banking, Credit, Finance, Financial, Fund, Investment, Insurance, Reinsurance, Trust, Trustee, Depository, Securities, Clearing, Settlement
Gibraltar Stock Exchange, GSE, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or authorized agent may file a formal appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the notice of rejection. The appeal must include the original name request, the rejection reason, a written submission explaining conformity with the Companies Act 2014 naming provisions, and any precedents of similar names already accepted by the Registry. The Registrar will issue a decision within 21 business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may reapply with a revised name or institute judicial review proceedings in the Gibraltar Supreme Court. In practice, most practitioners submit a fresh name reservation after an informal telephone or email consultation with the Registry to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Assessment of virtual office acceptance for this industry: A registered office in Gibraltar is statutorily required for every company under Section 43 of the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014. The registered office must be a physical address in Gibraltar. Virtual office service arrangements are permissible only if the provider operates a physical office facility in Gibraltar and provides commercial premises for receiving service of process, but the company must maintain substantive administrative presence adequate for the business. For a digital video chat application business, there is no requirement for a physical operational office at the pre-incorporation stage, but the registered office must be a genuine location staffed during business hours. The use of a virtual office alone will not satisfy economic substance if the company becomes subject to Gibraltar Economic Substance (ES) filing obligations under the Economic Substance Act, though in Stage 1 substance monitoring is not yet triggered. A licensed corporate service provider or law firm offering a virtual office will be treated as a registered office address, not as a trading presence. The regulator and banks will treat the virtual office as a 'care-of' arrangement and will require UBO, director, and employee records to remain at the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: 25% to 40% likelihood during the first 24 months of operation for a medium-risk non-licensed digital video application with cross-border payment rails and enhanced AML/CFT classification. If the company registers for a Gibraltar EMI-adjacent service, payment processing, or obtains a Financial Services permission (e.g., money service business), the likelihood increases to 65%. Given that the target business scope is a video chat social app using Apple IAP and Paymentwall, which does not require a financial services license, the statutory inspection risk is driven by AML/CFT regulation, data protection, and the physical registered office. Gibraltar supervisory authorities (Financial Intelligence Unit, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, Data Protection Commissioner) have unannounced inspection powers. In practice, an on-site inspection is likely only in the context of a broader AML/CFT compliance review or a substance assessment. For a standard pre-incorporation structure, physical inspection risk is assessed at 15% within the first 24 months and rising to 35% if the company begins to receive substantial cross-border payments without adequate substance or if it is selected at random under the supervision risk-based framework.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss. 8-18 (incorporation and registration of companies), s. 91 (registered office), ss. 108-116 (directors and company secretary); Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2015; Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar), Category 2 / Exempt Company classification, as applied to non-resident owned companies; Exempt Companies Rules (annual levy and non-residence declaration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies House - Registry of Companies, Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar (electronic filing window: Registry e-Filing; physical counter: 3-6 Secretary's Lane, Gibraltar).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association and Form GIB-INC-01 (Application for Registration of an Exempted Company), together with Form GIB-INC-02 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form GIB-INC-03 (Notice of First Directors and Secretary).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the exempted company may be incorporated with zero issued capital. No escrow, capital deposit, or proof of capital payment is required at formation, but the subscriber allotment of one ordinary share of no par value is recorded in the register of members upon incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company as a non-resident-owned exempted company under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 be ratified. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association be adopted and the allotment of one subscriber ordinary share of no par value be confirmed. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the offices of the licensed corporate services provider in Gibraltar, and that the directors and corporate secretary be appointed. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Board authorize execution of all incorporation and exempt-status filings, adoption of AML and money-laundering reporting obligations, opening of bank and EMI accounts, and signing of Apple IAP and Paymentwall merchant agreements. RESOLVED FURTHER, that each director be authorized to act singly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Clearance of Corporate Profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (Registration Pre-Clearance Desk) acted through a licensed Corporate Service Provider (CSP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Gibraltar-licensed CSP to submit up to three proposed company names through the Companies House name-check portal. Confirm that the proposed name does not contain prohibited or sensitive words (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Royal', 'University') and is distinct from existing registered names. Submit the name reservation request together with an accurate business description for the real-time video matching and cross-border social telephony platform so the Registry records the corporate object and exempt status at intake.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name variants (3 alternatives)
KYC / AML identification pack of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
Notarized passport and proof of residential address of the UBO
Business description for ISIC 6311 real-time video matching app services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as misleading or too similar, resubmit a new name variant within 5 business days; a written appeal for registry reconsideration may be filed under section 45 of the Companies Act 2014 within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Notary Public and licensed corporate counsel engaged by the CSP
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitutional documents in the approved Gibraltar exempt-company format, incorporating clauses on non-resident beneficial ownership, restriction from carrying on local Crown Dependencies business, permitted banking and treasury functions, and board authority over digital asset and payment service contracts. Execute the documents before a Gibraltar Notary Public, who certifies the signatures and affixes the notarial certificate. The CSP's compliance officer thereafter performs sanctions screening and issues the consent-to-act for the first directors.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association (Gov-GIB-MA-01)
Draft Articles of Association (Gov-GIB-ART-01)
Notarial certificate of execution and signature page
Consent-to-act forms of the first directors and corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries any constitutional clause (e.g., ambiguous restricted-business wording), amend the objected clause, re-execute the affected page before the notary, and refile a consolidated rectified copy within 7 calendar days with a covering explanation letter to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Application for Incorporation and Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies House (Registry e-Filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form GIB-INC-01 electronically together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, Form GIB-INC-02 (notice of registered office), and Form GIB-INC-03 (notice of first directors and secretary). Attach the statutory declaration of compliance confirming that all incorporation requirements have been satisfied and pay the applicable filing fee through the CSP's registry debit account. Retain the Registry acknowledgment with the assigned transactional reference.
required_dossiers: Form GIB-INC-01 signed by the subscriber
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form GIB-INC-02 registered office notice
Form GIB-INC-03 officer notices
Statutory declaration of compliance (Form GIB-INC-04)
Filing fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the CSP receives a Query Notice prescribing a 14-day cure period; rectify the statutory declaration, correct formatting or fee shortfalls, and resubmit. Failure to cure within the period results in deemed withdrawal, with fees refunded less an administrative charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and Grant of the Exempt Status Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies (issuance) and Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (exempt classification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registry satisfaction, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the unique company registration number. The CSP immediately files the exempt company application (CT-EXEMPT) with the Income Tax Office, attaching the non-residence declaration and proof that management and control occur outside Gibraltar, and pays the annual exempt-status levy. The Income Tax Office countersigns the Exempt Company Certificate or equivalent confirmation, and the CSP files the register of members and registered office confirmation in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Exempt company application (CT-EXEMPT) and non-residence declaration
Register of members and allotment record
UBO register opening page
Consent of registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If exempt status is challenged for lack of non-residence evidence, file a supplementary affidavit of the UBO and board minutes confirming offshore control within 21 days; an administrative review may be requested from the Commissioner of Income Tax within 30 days of any adverse decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Banking Onboarding, and Payment Rail Connectivity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House (records), Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (AML supervision of the CSP and payment institutions), and the chosen licensed bank or Electronic Money Institution (EMI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory post-registration steps: file the Beneficial Ownership filing under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2015, formally appoint the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO), adopt the AML/CTF risk assessment calibrated for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced video-chat social app, and hold the board meeting that ratifies the formation resolutions. Open a corporate transactional account with a Gibraltar-licensed bank or EMI, for execution of Apple IAP and Paymentwall merchant agreements; provide the bank with board resolutions, UBO structure, source-of-funds documentation, and a business narrative of the revenue model and content moderation framework.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and M&A
Duly filed Beneficial Ownership register
AML/KYC dossier of UBOs and directors
Board resolution for account opening and payment rail agreements
App store developer documentation and business model narrative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or EMI raises an enhanced due diligence query, respond within 10 business days with supplementary source-of-funds evidence, platform traffic analytics, and the Apple App Store / Paymentwall merchant verification certificates; in case of sustained refusal, apply to a secondary EMI or Gibraltar-licensed bank in the same banking consortium.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the real-time video matching service is classified as an over-the-top (OTT) digital application outside the licensing scope of the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority (GRA) under the Gibraltar Communications Act 2006; no sectoral industrial licence is administered by the GRA for ISIC 6311 software platform activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - no operating or manufacturing permit is prescribed for the video-chat social app; an ancillary Data Protection Registration (Controller Notification, RG150) with the Office of the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority under the Data Protection Act 2004 (Gibraltar) is mandatory for the processing of user personal data.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department for the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no full EIA or registration-level assessment is required because the undertaking operates from an office-only footprint with no manufacturing, process installation, or emissions point exceeding the de minimis thresholds of the Gibraltar Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations 2021.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-generated waste must be handled under the Environmental (Waste Management) Regulations 2012; electronic waste (servers, hardware) must be transferred to licensed waste carriers; no VOC, wastewater, or industrial effluent discharge arises from the digital services activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a Fire Safety Certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service for occupational use of the registered office premises, supported by a certified electrical installation inspection and a means-of-escape plan; file the workplace notification under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1997 (Gibraltar) and maintain the employers' liability certificate for all administrative staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office (ITO), HM Government of Gibraltar; corporate tax filings and registration are administered through the Government of Gibraltar tax portal and Gibraltar Companies House (www.gibraltar.gov.gi).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, the company automatically receives a unique Gibraltar company registration number (GRN), which serves as its corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN). The registered agent files a tax notification form with the Income Tax Office within 30 days of incorporation; the ITO then issues the corporate Tax Reference and annual self-assessment instructions. A foreign-controlled company seeking offshore tax treatment must additionally submit a formal Declaration of Central Management and Control evidencing that strategic management occurs outside Gibraltar. No separate TIN application is required for non-resident companies unless the entity later registers for local payroll (employer PAYE), customs, or a local establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — Gibraltar applies a territorial tax system: a company managed and controlled outside Gibraltar (non-resident/offshore) is chargeable only on income arising within Gibraltar. Foreign-source revenue from the video-match app (virtual credit sales, subscriptions, advertising, Apple IAP, Paymentwall settlements) falls outside the Gibraltar tax net. No capital gains tax is levied, and no Gibraltar withholding tax applies to dividends paid to non-residents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime. Available statutory mechanisms include: (i) elective non-residence treatment via evidence of central management and control abroad (board minutes, foreign meeting locations, key decision records); (ii) Group Relief election allowing surrender of losses within a 75% or more corporate group; (iii) small company fixed-rate assessment election for qualifying low-turnover companies; (iv) for in-scope MNE groups (consolidated revenue exceeding EUR 750 million), election to apply Gibraltar's Qualified Domestic Top-Up Tax at 15% and the Income Inclusion Rule under Pillar Two; and (v) redomiciliation/continuation election under the Companies Act to migrate the company's corporate seat out of Gibraltar without liquidation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT / GST / Sales Tax. Gibraltar is excluded from the UK VAT system and the EU VAT area. Indirect taxation is limited to Gibraltar Import Duties and Excise Duties on specific physical goods (tobacco, alcohol, hydrocarbons). Online digital services supplied by the company are not subject to any Gibraltar indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST registration threshold exists in Gibraltar because no such tax is levied. For customs purposes, a physical importer of dutiable goods (alcohol, tobacco, fuel) must register with the Gibraltar Customs Service from the first import (effective threshold: GBP 0). Purely digital turnover creates no customs or indirect-tax registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandate. Gibraltar does not operate real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoice clearance, digital stamping, or API-based tax reporting. Voluntary e-invoicing is commercially permissible. Physical imports/exports, when made, require electronic customs declarations via the Gibraltar Customs Service single window (compatible with UK CDS documentation formats), but this is a customs/border process and not a tax-invoicing obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is not applicable as a VAT concept because Gibraltar imposes no VAT/GST. All digital services supplied to non-resident users are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax (effectively 0%). Physical goods exported from Gibraltar are generally free of export duty, provided the goods physically depart and are supported by customs evidence. Input VAT refunds cannot be claimed in Gibraltar (no input VAT exists); any foreign VAT incurred (e.g., EU cloud hosting, SaaS procurement) must be reclaimed through the relevant foreign jurisdiction's recovery mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Gibraltar Single Administrative Document / electronic export declaration) — required only for physical goods; digital-only operations rely on payment and transaction records
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (logistics provider certificate of export) — required for physical consignments; not required for pure digital B2C services
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/PSP settlement statement (SWIFT MT103, Apple IAP, Paymentwall payout statements) evidencing receipt of foreign currency from non-resident users
Transaction-level audit log with user geolocation (IP country), device metadata, and app-store settlement summaries linking each revenue stream to foreign markets
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar Income Tax Office may open audit inquiries within six years from the end of the chargeable period (unlimited in fraud cases). If the company fails to evidence non-resident management and control or foreign-source revenue, the ITO may recharacterise profits as Gibraltar-source and assess tax at the standard 12.5% corporate rate, plus late-payment interest. Under the Income Tax Act 2010, penalties for incorrect returns range from 50% (careless) to 100% of tax understated (deliberate with concealment); fraudulent claims attract criminal sanctions. No VAT clawback exists, but false customs export declarations are sanctioned under the Customs Ordinance through forfeiture of goods, fines up to GBP 5,000, and loss of duty-free export privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar does not maintain a domestic central bank. The Government of Gibraltar issues the Gibraltar pound (GIP) under the Currency Notes Act 1934 at a fixed 1:1 parity with the British pound; banking supervision is vested in the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC); and the Bank of England provides the underlying monetary framework. For the underlying Bermuda Exempted Company, the Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) administers the Exchange Control Act 1972 and regulates the exchange-control classification of the entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility with no exchange controls, fixed-peg GIP/GBP parity, and unrestricted profit repatriation by dividends, management fees, loan repayments, or liquidation distributions. The operating treasury route from a Gibraltar account to Bermuda or international counterparties is free of central-bank approval hurdles. On the Bermuda layer, the Exempted Company must be designated as non-resident for exchange-control purposes (a permitted-entity classification is typically granted by the BMA), which fully exempts USD/EUR digital-export proceeds from convertibility requirements and removes any remittance obstacle for shareholder distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Neither Gibraltar nor Bermuda imposes statutory export-proceeds surrender timelines or mandatory conversion ratios. Digital service revenues (ISIC 6311; Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlements) may be retained indefinitely in USD, EUR, or GBP, converted at market rates at the corporate treasury's discretion, and redeployed without central-bank reporting thresholds in Gibraltar. The corresponding Bermuda requirement is only an exchange-control non-resident status filing, ensuring that collections are not obliged to be sold to an authorised dealer; ordinary financial-return filings to the Bermuda Registrar remain the sole periodic compliance duty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for cross-border fintech/EMI sponsorship. Legal constraints: after the UK's departure from the EU, UK-authorised electronic money institutions no longer automatically passport into Gibraltar; any EMI activity requires a Gibraltar licence under the Financial Services (Electronic Money) Act 2011, including a physical establishment and a local MLRO. The Bermuda Exempted Company is unlikely to meet the commercial onboarding criteria of offshore digital EMIs such as Revolut, Wise, or Airwallex because these firms impose geographic-presence restrictions, beneficial-ownership profile limitations, and often decline Bermuda-Exempted corporate structures. The practical approach is a GFSC-licensed bank account at a Tier-1 bank with an API/treasury digitisation layer, while keeping Paymentwall as a collection concentrator rather than a bank substitute.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar licensed banks generally require at least one full in-person interview of a director or the ultimate beneficial owner, or exceptionally permit remote onboarding through video-link KYC supplemented by an apostilled board resolution, notarised passports, independent bank references, and a Gibraltar law-firm introducer. For a Random Video Match social-telephony app with a foreign corporate structure, the MLRO will normally insist on a physical signature appointment in Gibraltar, because the proposed account is a medium-risk enhanced file; remote-only opening is reserved for verified low-risk entities, and the enhanced due-diligence profile of the digital-services sector eliminates that presumption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector reputation red flag: random video-match and cross-border social telephony apps are misclassified as anonymous-chat channels with adult-content, online-grooming, and misuse exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) a detailed business-model and data-flow narrative; (ii) user ID verification, age-gating, geoblocking, and 24/7 AI content-moderation documentation; (iii) Apple IAP and Paymentwall merchant agreements evidencing prohibited-content contractual safeguards; (iv) GDPR/DPA 2018 privacy notices, Terms of Use, and child-safety safeguards; (v) a signed compliance manual, doing-business acceptance policy, and the board's resolution authorising transparent cooperation with the GFSC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional ambiguity: a non-resident Bermuda Exempted Company with no local substance triggers bank intake alarm on economic-substance, tax-motivation, and UBO transparency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) the Bermuda Certificate of Exemption and current statutory declarations; (ii) a BMA-filed Beneficial Ownership register extract and an ownership-chain chart; (iii) an economic-substance (ESR) assessment and any permitted tax-residence confirmation; (iv) Gibraltar registered-office, corporate-service-provider, and directors' identity records; (v) an audited opening balance sheet evidencing real capitalisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement profile: high-frequency, high-volume inflows from aggregators (Apple IAP, Paymentwall) with thin invoice trail may be flagged as transaction-laundering or mule-account facilitation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) three years of audited financial statements or the most recent interim review and a 12-month cash-flow forecast; (ii) Apple and Paymentwall settlement and payout statements with net commissions, refunds, and tax-withholding detail; (iii) an IFRS 15/ASC 606 revenue-recognition memo; (iv) a transactional-monitoring system description with sanctions and PEP screening; (v) chargeback and fraud-management sub-policies with a documented dispute-containment procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High chargeback/refund ratio around recurring IAP subscriptions could be interpreted by the bank as an indicator of fraud laundering or poor consumer-protection governance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present (i) the chargeback-management and refund-control standard operating procedure; (ii) card-network performance evidence (e.g., Visa/Mastercard chargeback-rate reports or waiver/consolidation notices); (iii) customer onboarding and in-app payment consent trail; (iv) customer complaints log and first-response SLA metrics; (v) PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation of compliance and the merchant acquirer's written risk assessment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions will be injected via SWIFT MT103 from the Bermuda Exempted Company's Bermudian corporate bank account (or from the UBO's private wealth account) into the Gibraltar escrow/operational account using ISO 20022 purpose code EQUITY or CAPC with the shareholder meeting minute and allotment resolution referenced in the SWIFT remittance field. The pre-funding verification pack includes a board capital-call resolution, a share-register excerpt, a source-of-wealth statement, notarised KYC of the remitter and recipient, and written pre-clearance from the Gibraltar bank's onboarding team confirming the exact coded instruction. UK Faster Payments applies exclusively to domestic GBP payments and CHAPS to high-value GBP settlement; inbound USD/EUR flows use SWIFT correspondents, with expected delivery windows of one to two business days and no capital-import licence requirement under Gibraltar law.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Contractor, vendor, and operational disbursements use SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.002) for cross-border settlements, SEPA Instant/SEPA Credit for euro-area recipients, and UK Faster Payments for suppliers holding UK sort codes. High-volume micro-disbursements (creator/affiliate payouts) are consolidated into daily batched clearing files to reduce corridor charges. For the procurement of hardware, media placement, or licence-based technology assets, a standard irrevocable or standby commercial letter of credit may be issued via the Gibraltar bank's Trade Services desk; however, the default expected clearing rail for service-based trade is direct MT103/TT with original invoice and contract references, matching the merchant settlement reports from Apple and Paymentwall.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/GBP, EUR/GBP, and GIP/GBP) up to 12-month tenors under an ISDA 2002 or local bank master agreement, fully covered by underlying forecast settlement flows from Apple IAP and Paymentwall

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible user-market currencies (INR, IDR, TRY, EGP) executed only with a GFSC-approved counterparty and in no sanctioned jurisdiction, used to hedge local-language consumer revenue risk
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR/GBP) aligned to intercompany loans and capital-escrow balances between the Bermuda Exempted Company and the Gibraltar operating treasury
FX spot and rolling-spot conversions within a board-approved daily value-at-risk loss limit
Zero-cost collars (range forwards) for EUR/GBP and USD/GBP volatility, on a deliverable and documented basis

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return (Form 2) and Certificate of Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 January; each return covers the calendar year ending on the preceding 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a BMD 250 late fee plus potential BMD 1,000 restoration fee; continuing default allows the Bermuda Registrar to strike the exempted company off the register after 90 days of public notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Overseas Company Annual Return (Gibraltar) with Home-Jurisdiction Annual Return Attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 calendar days after the anniversary of registration as an overseas company in Gibraltar; where the Bermuda annual return is prepared on a calendar-year basis, no later than 31 March each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating late filing penalties: GBP 15 up to 1 month, GBP 50 up to 3 months, GBP 100 up to 6 months, GBP 750 over 12 months; persistent default enables the Gibraltar Registrar to strike the overseas company registration from the Register of Overseas Companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Annual Confirmation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after filing the annual return and in any event before 30 June each year; UBO changes, including shareholding transfers, must be reported within 14 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is a criminal offence: fine up to GBP 25,000 plus daily default fine of GBP 500; directors and officers may be disqualified for serious breaches.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (Gibraltar Foreign Company Branch Filing, where threshold exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year for an overseas company registered in Gibraltar; if the company qualifies for small-company audit exemption, a signed statement of qualifying conditions may be filed instead.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late delivery of accounts is a criminal offence by the company and each officer; court fine up to GBP 5,000 per officer, civil penalties up to GBP 5,000, and disqualification of up to 5 years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is compulsory in Gibraltar unless the company qualifies as small under two or more of the following criteria: annual turnover not over GBP 10.2 million, balance sheet total not over GBP 5.1 million, average employees not over 50. Bermuda exempted companies in private ownership are generally exempt from statutory audit unless listed on a securities exchange or otherwise designated as a public-interest entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Gibraltar for statutory accounts; US GAAP or IFRS as permitted by Bermuda law for the Bermuda exempted company; both frameworks must produce a true and fair presentation after audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: On an annual basis, the Bermuda exempted company must confirm the accuracy of its beneficial ownership register by filing a Certificate of Compliance with the Bermuda Registrar. In Gibraltar, the overseas company must submit UBO confirmation through the Companies Registry, including all shareholding transfers completed during the year; any transfer notification is due within 14 days of completion. Failure to update the UBO register after a share transfer makes the company and officers liable to criminal penalties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 (Bermuda registered office and resident secretary plus Gibraltar registered agent and registered office services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 35,000 (certified auditors in Bermuda and Gibraltar for a cross-border digital platform company with modest intra-group transactions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory exemption from Gibraltar corporate income tax for qualifying exempted companies deriving no Gibraltar-source income; standard headline rate is 10% for taxable resident companies; no VAT, no capital gains tax, no branch remittance tax, and no dividend withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CR-200A Exempt Company Annual Return, filed electronically via the Gibraltar Income Tax Office eTax Portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the financial year; a 31 December year-end requires submission by 30 June of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company full legal name, Gibraltar registration number, and Tax File Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Bermuda Exempted Company name as registered in Gibraltar; identify with legal form code 'BMEX' for non-resident exempt undertaking

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start date and end date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the accounting period adopted by the Bermuda-exempted company; if central management and control are outside Gibraltar, still align with the Gibraltar statutory year for filing purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residency status declaration: Resident Taxable, Resident Exempt, or Non-Resident Exempt
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select 'Non-Resident Exempt' if board meetings and strategic decisions take place outside Gibraltar, e.g., Bermuda or the UK; otherwise select 'Resident Exempt' under the Qualifying Companies Act
Declare only income arising from Gibraltar customers or payments sourced in Gibraltar; zero-code all cross-border mobile application revenue collected through Apple IAP and Paymentwall

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source commercial income excluded from territorial taxation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide gross receipts from real-time video matching and social telephony; affirm no Gibraltar nexus; attach a brief economic substance explanation
Compute transfer-pricing-adjusted EBITDA at arm's length, including any inter-company fees, then apply the foreign-source exclusion to reduce taxable profit to nil

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: DTA relief and foreign tax credit schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where a DTA such as the UK-Gibraltar arrangement applies, upload the Gibraltar Tax Residence Certificate (TRC), foreign WHT certificates, and a schedule of foreign taxes suffered

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorizing officer, director, or resident agent declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The form must be digitally signed by a director authorized by the Board; for non-resident companies, a Gibraltar resident agent may countersign without assuming tax liability

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form CR-200A triggers a fixed penalty of GIP 300 plus a daily extension penalty of GIP 30 up to a maximum GIP 4,500; negligent or fraudulent returns attract a 100% tax shortfall penalty and criminal fines up to GIP 100,000; continued default can lead to company strike-off and director disqualification orders

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Gibraltar does not impose dividend withholding tax, but to invoke treaty benefits under the UK-Gibraltar DTA or other agreements, the company must obtain a Gibraltar Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the Commissioner of Income Tax, complete the relevant treaty claim form (e.g., Form DT-S), file it with the paying agent before remittance, and retain evidence of beneficial ownership; if treaty tax has been over-withheld, a repayment claim must be filed within two years of the end of the tax year in which the income arose.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and debt interest paid by a Gibraltar entity to non-residents is 0%; under the UK-Gibraltar DTA, the treaty rate for interest and royalties also reduces to 0%, subject to the recipient's beneficial ownership status, TRC, and anti-abuse limitation clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GIP 1,000,000 annual aggregate of controlled transactions triggers mandatory Local File; GIP 3,500,000 annual group turnover triggers a Master File; de minimis exemption below GIP 250,000 per related-party transaction; any cross-border transaction with a no-tax or exempted affiliate must be documented regardless of value.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Under Gibraltar's Companies (Economic Substance) Act and the International Tax Compliance (Economic Substance) Regulations, entities claiming the 0% exempt status must maintain adequate substance in Gibraltar for 'Geographically Mobile Business', including board meetings, qualified employees, physical assets, and core income-generating activities; a Bermuda Exempted Company conducting real-time video chat and social telephony must demonstrate real decision-making in Gibraltar or face denial of exemption, penalties up to GIP 100,000, and forced striking-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing global revenue streams from the video-chat app; reporting zero overseas income while Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlements are diverted to Bermuda bank accounts; or falsely claiming non-residence while management and control are exercised from London.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty equal to 200% of the undercharged tax; criminal conviction for evasion under the Income Tax Act carrying a fine of up to GIP 100,000 and imprisonment up to seven years; interest accrues at the standard late-payment rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute or conspire in the evasion are personally liable for the unpaid taxes through piercing the corporate veil; courts may impose asset freezing, travel bans, and imprisonment between 12 months and seven years; disqualification from being a director for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Bermuda Exempted Company label with no website, no office, no staff, no board meeting minutes, and no active management; all app development and operations are outsourced to third-party developers in China or Eastern Europe, while Gibraltar is used solely to secure a tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance Office levies penalties from GIP 10,000 to GIP 100,000 per infringement; the tax exemption is retroactively revoked, causing reassessment at 10% for six years, plus interest and penalties; applicable laws: Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2021.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for back taxes and penalties; in severe substance failures, the court can grant a 'fraudulent trading' order making directors personally liable for all company debts under section 332 of the Companies Act 2014.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging inflated management fees or royalty payments to the Gibraltar operating entity to shift profits into the Bermuda exempted parent; failing to prepare a contemporaneous bench-marking study; or engaging in circular invoicing through Paymentwall to avoid controlled-transaction recognition.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority makes an arm's-length adjustment increasing taxable income; penalty of 100% of any understated tax plus 2% monthly interest; separate documentation penalties up to GIP 25,000 for non-production of Local File and Master File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Finance directors and TP signatories face strict liability under the Transfer Pricing and Substance Regulations; personal penalties are imposed where misstatements are knowingly false, including personal fines up to GIP 50,000 and prohibition from holding financial management roles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a real-time video-matching app without verifying the identity of users; accepting proceeds from anonymous in-app purchases via Apple IAP and Paymentwall; and funneling 'virtual gifts' into bank accounts without implementing risk-based anti-money-laundering procedures under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial Intelligence Unit imposes penalties up to GIP 250,000 or 5% of annual turnover, whichever is higher; senior officers can be imprisoned for up to two years; the company's designated interested business licence may be revoked, blocking App Store collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for conspiracy to launder money; they may be subject to worldwide travel bans, asset seizure, and custodial sentences of up to 14 years; corporate veil-piercing applies where the company is an instrumentality for illicit funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Dividend Stripping and Illegal Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends in favor of the Bermuda shareholder while the Gibraltar entity has no distributable reserves, or paying out without a solvency certificate; failing to report the distribution as a gross payment in the annual return to preserve the exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil restitution order: directors must repay any distribution made from capital to the company; the distribution is disallowed for tax-exemption purposes, resulting in a 10% corporate tax charge and late-payment penalties; potential strike-off proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director who voted for an unlawful dividend is jointly and severally liable to restore the amount to the company; fraudulent intended concealment may lead to extradition-eligible offenses and director disqualification for up to 15 years.
